_strings.@@53a3b0ee8333: Treaty conformity — VA conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from VA income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the VA return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Virginia's individual income tax computation starts from federal adjusted gross income (Form 760, Line 1: "Enter the federal adjusted gross income from your federal return... use the federal adjusted gross income amount, NOT federal taxable income"). Virginia's official Additions list and Schedule ADJ contain NO addback for income exempt from federal tax under a U.S. tax treaty or for treaty-excluded foreign income (additions are limited to items like interest on other states' obligations, bonus depreciation, federally-exempt U.S. obligations interest, etc.). Because treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI and Virginia does not add it back, it flows through and is NOT re-taxed -> conforms.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: Form 760 Line 16: "Amount of Tax from Tax Table or Tax Rate Schedule (round to whole dollars)". Instructions, Line 16 Amount of Tax: "To compute your tax, you can use either the tax table or the tax rate schedule on Page 35, or use the Tax Calculator on the Department's website." Line 15 Virginia Taxable Income = Line 9 (VAGI) minus Line 14 (Line 10 itemized OR Line 11 standard deduction, + Line 12 exemptions + Line 13 Schedule ADJ deductions). Verified exemption kinds shipped but NOT applied by this op (compute them on the form): age_65 ($800 — Exemption Section B: 'Multiply the sum of exemptions claimed for 65 or older and Blind by $800.' Must be 65 or older on or before January 1, 2024. A base reduction via Line 12, but NOT applied by calc.state_tax (engine applies only personal/dependent keys) — claim it on the form. Cannot be claimed if the Credit for Low-Income Individuals is claimed on Line 23.); blind ($800 — Exemption Section B: $800 per blind exemption (blind for federal income tax purposes; taxpayer and spouse each). A base reduction via Line 12, but NOT applied by calc.state_tax — claim it on the form. Cannot be claimed if the Credit for Low-Income Individuals is claimed on Line 23.) This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply Form 760 Line 9, Virginia Adjusted Gross Income (VAGI) = federal AGI (Line 1, 'Adjusted Gross Income from federal return - Not federal taxable income') + Virginia additions (Line 2, Schedule ADJ Line 3) - Line 8 subtractions (Line 4 age deduction, Line 5 taxable Social Security/Tier 1 Railroad Retirement benefits, Line 6 state income tax refund reported as federal income, Line 7 Schedule ADJ subtractions). If the filer has no Virginia additions or subtractions, VAGI equals federal AGI. The op then subtracts the shipped $930-per-exemption amounts and the per-status standard deduction to reproduce Virginia taxable income (Line 15 = Line 9 - Line 14). Adjudication note (two-pass): base is federal_agi — Form 760 line 1 is federal adjusted gross income and Line 9 VAGI = federal AGI +/- Virginia additions/subtractions; supply Line 9 (the op subtracts the standard deduction and $930-per-exemption amounts). Single rate schedule for ALL filing statuses: Virginia publishes one 2023 Tax Rate Schedule (2% to $3,000; $60 + 3% $3,000-$5,000; $120 + 5% $5,000-$17,000; $720 + 5.75% over $17,000) that applies regardless of filing status; it is duplicated per status here. The printed constants $60/$120/$720 exactly equal the cumulative sums of the prior brackets — no rounding divergence. Virginia filing statuses are only 1 = Single, 2 = Joint, 3 = Married Filing Separately. Head of Household is NOT a separate Virginia status: 'Fill in the Head of Household oval if your filing status is Single and you checked the Head of Household box on your federal return' — HOH filers use Filing Status 1 (Single) and the $8,000 standard deduction, which is what this pack ships for head_of_household. ZERO-TAX FILING THRESHOLD not applied by the engine: Form 760 Line 9 prints 'Note: If less than $11,950 for Filing Status 1 or 3; or $23,900 for Filing Status 2, your tax is $0.00', and the rate-schedule page instructs 'If your Virginia Adjusted Gross Income is less than the filing threshold, do not use the rate schedule or tax table below. Enter $0 as your tax instead.' If VAGI is below the threshold, the correct Virginia tax is $0 even though bracket math yields a positive number. Tax table: Virginia's tax table (booklet pp.35-43, covering taxable income up to $98,356) is OPTIONAL, not mandated — 'The tax table can be used if your Virginia taxable income is listed in the table. Otherwise, use the Tax Rate Schedule.' Within table bands the table (band-midpoint based) may differ from exact bracket math by about $1; Line 16 permits the table, the rate schedule, or the Department's online Tax Calculator. Spouse Tax Adjustment (STA) NOT modeled: couples filing jointly (Filing Status 2) may reduce their tax by up to $259 on Form 760 Line 17 if both spouses have taxable income and combined taxable income exceeds $3,000 (STA Worksheet, booklet p.13). The engine computes Line 16 only; a joint filer's Line 18 net tax may be up to $259 lower. Age 65+/blind exemptions ($800 each, Exemption Section B) are base reductions included in Line 12 but are NOT applied by calc.state_tax (the op applies only the personal/dependent keys) — enter them on the form. They cannot be claimed together with the Credit for Low-Income Individuals. Age Deduction (Line 4, up to $12,000 per qualifying taxpayer, birth-date- and income-based per the Age Deduction Worksheet) and the Line 5 Social Security / Tier 1 Railroad Retirement subtraction, Line 6 state refund subtraction, and Line 7 Schedule ADJ subtractions are all taken BEFORE VAGI — the caller must supply Form 760 Line 9 already reflecting them. Itemizers: 'If you claimed itemized deductions on your federal return' you MUST itemize on the Virginia return (Line 10, Virginia Schedule A) and the standard deduction does not apply — the shipped standard_deduction is only for standard-deduction filers. Under Filing Status 3, if one spouse itemizes the other must also itemize. Dependent on another's return: the standard deduction is limited to the amount of earned income ('Enter the smaller of the amount of earned income or the standard deduction amount on Line 11') — not modeled. The 2023 standard deduction amounts ($8,000 single/MFS, $16,000 MFJ) come from 2022 General Assembly legislation that raised them for Taxable Year 2023 (from $4,500/$9,000); the increase is scheduled to sunset after Taxable Year 2025. Credit for Low-Income Individuals ($300 per exemption), the nonrefundable Virginia EITC (20% of federal EITC), and the refundable Virginia EITC (15%) are CREDITS subtracted from tax on Form 760 Line 23 via Schedule ADJ Line 17 — they are NOT exemptions and are not modeled by this op. Rounding: Virginia rounds to whole dollars with 50-99 cents rounding up; the booklet's own rate-schedule example rounds $4,917.50 to $4,918, matching the engine's half-up rounding. Qualifying surviving spouse: the engine maps QSS to married_filing_jointly. The 2023 booklet lists only Filing Statuses 1/2/3 and does not explicitly state which status a federal QSS filer uses; because Virginia has a single rate schedule, only the standard deduction ($16,000 vs $8,000) would differ — confirm the correct status at tax.virginia.gov.
